rows.name: Small Mario - standing/facing right, 2x2 CHR metasprite (blank-padded 16x32 OAM form), sprite palette 4
rows.notes:
list_sprites proves the block: 8 OAM entries (slots 1-8) all sprite palette 4, no vertical flips, none behind background; slots 5-8 carry the visible 16x16 and slots 1-4 are the blank $FC filler of the 16x32 sprite form. Origin = top-left of the visible 16x16 at screen (40,193) in the World 1-1 opening frame (CHR pattern table 0 / sprite table $0000). OAM entries as (tile id, x offset, y offset, flips):
- $FC (252), (+0,-16), none - blank filler
- $FC (252), (+8,-16), none - blank filler
- $FC (252), (+0,-8), none - blank filler
- $FC (252), (+8,-8), none - blank filler
- $3A (58), (+0,+0), none - upper-left (hat top + face/hair)
- $37 (55), (+8,+0), none - upper-right (hat brim + face)
- $4F (79), (+0,+8), none - lower-left (shirt/overalls/hand/shoe)
- $4F (79), (+8,+8), flip_h (attr $40) - lower-right (mirror of lower-left)
Slot 0 of OAM (tile $FF at (88,25), palette 7) is the HUD coin icon, not Mario. Note the sprite-form origin is (40,177): the four $FC entries sit at y 177/185, above the drawn pixels.
rows.why: OAM $3A/$37 over $4F/$4F(h) under four $FC fillers, palette 4; rendered from sprite CHR they are small Mario standing, as drawn at (40,193)

rows.name: small_mario sprite palette (slot1 $16 red hat+shirt, slot2 $27 orange skin, slot3 $18 olive hair/eyes/shoes)
rows.notes: Sprite palette 4, live value [15, 22, 39, 24] = [$0F, $16, $27, $18] (get_all_palettes). Slot 0 = $0F: sprite index 0 is transparent, never drawn. Slot 1 = $16 red: Mario's hat (top and brim) and his shirt/overalls. PROOF: write_palette(4, index 1) -> $2C cyan and step_frame 2 turned the hat and the whole body cyan while the face stayed orange (screenshot); clear_palette_overrides restored $16, and the rendered pixels read $16 at (45,194) and (49,194) again. Slot 2 = $27 orange: his skin, the face and the hands - sampled rendered $27 at (45,199) and (43,203), which are exactly the CHR index-2 pixels of tiles $3A/$37/$4F. Slot 3 = $18 olive: the dark detail - hair, eyes/mustache and shoes (the CHR index-3 pixels of those tiles). In the World 1-1 opening screen palette 4 is used by Mario's metasprite only (the OAM slot-0 HUD coin icon and the Goomba use palette 7).
rows.why: after slot 1 was written $2C, the 45 red pixels of Mario's cap and body are cyan in this screenshot and face/hair are unchanged; slot 1 cap/body, 2 skin, 3 hair/eyes/shoes as claimed

rows.name: bush body fill (solid middle of the base)
rows.notes: CHR $125 (BG pattern table $1000, nametable tile id $25): all 64 pixels are palette index 1 - a solid lime-green block, the flat middle of the bush's base. Placed six times in nametable 0 row 25 (y 200-207) cols 24-29 of the World 1-1 opening screen. BG palette 0 slot 1 = $29 lime green. Proof: get_region object mode at (210,198) returned this CHR id inside the 709-pixel bush region (background palette 0, slots 1,2,3, box (184,192)-(241,207), window anchored (178,166)); read_tile(293) shows a uniform index-1 grid.
rows.why: CHR $135/$138 are the bush's rounded ends, $136/$137 the bump halves, $125 the fill (rendered from the ROM); the bush at the right of the screenshot

rows.name: bush bottom-left (left slope + left outline of the base)
rows.notes: CHR $135 (BG pattern table $1000, nametable tile id $35): index-1 lime fill whose top surface slopes down to the left (black index-3 outline from (7,0) to (2,3)) with a short black outline down the left side (col 0, rows 4-6). It is the bush's left end, sitting one tile to the LEFT of the hump row, so its top-left is exposed. Placed once in nametable 0 col 23 row 25 (y 200-207) of the World 1-1 opening screen. Proof: get_region object mode at (210,198) lists CHR 0x135 among the bush tiles (palette 0).

The bush's right end, one tile to the RIGHT of the hump row. Placed once in nametable 0 col 30 row 25 (y 200-207) of the World 1-1 opening screen. Proof: get_region object mode at (210,198) lists CHR 0x138 among the bush tiles (palette 0).

rows.name: bush top-left (left half of a scallop/hump)
rows.notes: CHR $136 (BG pattern table $1000, nametable tile id $36): black index-3 outline running from its top-right corner down-left (top-right (6,0)-(7,0) to (2,3)) then down the left side, index-1 lime fill to its right, plus index-2 green shading at the lower right (row 6 cols 4-5, row 7 col 4). It forms the LEFT half of one scallop of the bush's top: placed three times in nametable 0 row 24 (y 192-199) cols 24, 26, 28, each followed immediately by a $137 so the two outlines meet in a peak at the tile boundary (three humps total). rows.name: Status-bar layout (MARIO/score, coin, WORLD, TIME) in nametable 0 rows 2-3
rows.notes:
Super Mario Bros. status bar is fixed background in nametable 0, tile rows 2-3 (screen y 16-31); rows 0-1 (y 0-15) are sky tile $24. Same layout on the title screen and in World 1-1. PROOF: read_nametable NT0 (0,2) 32x2 plus screenshots of both.

ROW 2 = labels (all BG palette 2):
- MARIO: cols 3-7 = tiles $16,$0A,$1B,$12,$18 (M,A,R,I,O).
- WORLD: cols 18-22 = tiles $14,$18,$1B,$15,$0D (W,O,R,L,D).
- TIME: cols 25-28 = tiles $1D,$12,$16,$0E (T,I,M,E).

ROW 3 = numbers:
- Score: cols 3-8, six digit tiles (here 00 00 00 = "000000").
- Coin icon: NOT background - an OAM sprite, slot 0, tile $FF, palette 7, at screen (88,25) = tile col 11 row 3 (list_sprites).
- "x" sign: col 12 = tile $29 (CHR $129).
- Coin count: cols 13-14 = tens then ones digit tiles (here 00).
- World number: col 19 = world digit, col 20 = dash tile $28 (CHR $128), col 21 = level digit (here $01,$28,$01 = "1-1").
- TIME digits: cols 26-28 = hundreds, tens, ones (here blank $24 on the title; in 1-1 e.g. $03,$06,$07 = "367").

The score 6 tiles at cols 3-8 carry the digits of $07DD-$07E2; coin cols 13-14 carry $07ED/$07EE; TIME cols 26-28 carry $07F8-$07FA. All HUD background tiles sit in BG palette 2 (attribute block cols 8-11 near the coin holds palette 3 but the tiles there are sky).
rows.why: two errors against the screenshot and the nametable: WORLD's W is tile $20, not $14, and the coin icon at col 11 is background tile $2E (the hidden $FF sprite sits behind it), not a sprite
